items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: But that was a club that was booking with Sonny Stitt one week and then Jimmy Cavallo

ctx.x: What did being “on the road” constitute? Like one nighters in dance clubs?

No, well like depending on which band I was with — I went on the road with Jimmy Cavallo and we were playing weeklong engagements. We were like a week at the Thunderbird Lounge and wherever, New Bedford, Massachusetts, the Piccadilly Lounge. I remember they used to have a tank of piranha that was the high point of the evening, because we’d play on top of the bar and the bartender would feed the piranha something. I don’t know what he was feeding them, goldfish I guess. And that was fun. But that was a club that…

you know, like you’re hearing the syncopation. I see an eighth note and it’s like baDA, not bada. You know, so that kind of thing. So I wasn’t really locked into that. Now I quit Jimmy Cavallo’s band and went back with the Salt City Six for a couple of years I guess. And we were traveling doing Florida, and I don’t remember the places, whatever they were. And those were nice jobs. But in 1965 Vietnam was heating up.
